page.overview:
What is Goron?

The (pronounced ), also known as the Goron Tribe, are a race of rock people inhabiting Hyrule, Termina, and several other countries, typically living in mountain ranges. They have been called "rock people" since ancient times, when the goddess Hylia ruled and have long held close ties with the Hyrulean royal family. They have the capability to thrive in any environment, and in times of crisis, have survived by migrating to different climes. They are notable for having a lack of identifiable female members, nearly the polar opposite of the Gerudo race. The race made their first appearance in .

The Gorons are a large, muscular, mountain-dwelling race, with sizes ranging from medium, tall, and even gigantic. The largest known Goron in series is Biggoron, who is roughly about the same height as the peak of Death Mountain. Goron legs are short, especially in comparison to their much longer arms. Some also live on islands, such as on Goron Island. Befitting with that of their habitat, their durable, round bodies greatly resemble that of stones and boulders, and nearly all Gorons have a hide of ridged stones on their backsides. They usually have light brown skin. The Gorons have small eyes and noticeable lips, which conceal unaligned, square teeth. Another common trait are their symbols in the shape of the Spiritual Stone of Fire, Goron's Ruby, tattooed to the sides of their arms. Whether this is natural or not is unknown. Combined with their round shape, Gorons can also curl themselves into a ball shape and roll like a boulder, which is also their primary attack against enemies.

To date, no female members of this race have been seen at any point in the long-running series. Gorons are born from the earth itself, and refer to other Gorons who were born in the same place as them as their own siblings.

Also known as: Gorons.
